facts.fact: In the 2024 election cycle, campaigns spent $2.3 billion on CTV advertising, representing 21% of total political ad spend (AdImpact via NBC News).
facts.quote: In the 2024 election cycle, campaigns spent $2.3 billion on CTV advertising, representing 21% of total political ad spend

facts.fact: The 2026 midterm cycle is projected to see over $10.8 billion in political ad spending, more than 20% higher than 2022 (AdImpact via OpenSecrets).
facts.quote: The 2026 midterm cycle is projected to see over $10.8 billion in political ad spending, more than 20% higher than 2022

facts.fact: 88% of U.S. households own at least one connected TV device (Leichtman Research Group, 2024).
facts.quote: 88% of U.S. households now own at least one connected TV device

facts.fact: Streaming accounted for 41.4% of all TV viewing time according to Nielsen's The Gauge, January 2025.
facts.quote: streaming now accounts for 41.4% of all TV viewing time ([Nielsen, The Gauge, January 2025]

facts.fact: Industry-wide voter file to CTV match rates typically fall between 50% and 80%, depending on voter file quality and onboarding platform (LiveRamp, 2024).
facts.quote: voter file to CTV match rates typically fall between 50% and 80%, depending on the quality of the voter file and the onboarding platform used

facts.fact: Some campaigns report match rates above 85% when using high-quality, recently updated files with multiple match keys.
facts.quote: Some campaigns report match rates above 85% when using high-quality, recently updated files with multiple match keys.

facts.fact: A congressional candidate in a suburban district might pay for 500,000 impressions when only 50,000 reach actual district voters, per the guide's illustrative example.
facts.quote: A congressional candidate in a suburban district might pay for 500,000 impressions when only 50,000 reach actual district voters.

facts.fact: Adwave's table shows a 60% match rate for a 50,000-voter file, yielding about 30,000 targetable households.
facts.quote: | 50,000 voters | 60% | ~30,000 households |

facts.fact: Adwave's table shows a 65% match rate for a 100,000-voter file, yielding about 65,000 targetable households.
facts.quote: | 100,000 voters | 65% | ~65,000 households |

facts.fact: Adwave's table shows a 70% match rate for a 250,000-voter file, yielding about 175,000 targetable households.
facts.quote: | 250,000 voters | 70% | ~175,000 households |

facts.fact: Adwave's table shows a 75% match rate for a 500,000-voter file, yielding about 375,000 targetable households.
facts.quote: | 500,000 voters | 75% | ~375,000 households |

facts.fact: According to LiveRamp (2024), email-based matching alone can yield 70-80% match rates when emails are available.
facts.quote: Email-based matching alone can yield 70-80% match rates when emails are available

facts.fact: Traditional data onboarding required minimum media commitments of $50,000 to $100,000 or more, per Adwave's description.
facts.quote: Traditional data onboarding required minimum media commitments of $50,000 to $100,000 or more.

facts.fact: Adwave states the traditional onboarding process itself could cost $10,000 to $25,000 in platform fees and data costs.
facts.quote: The onboarding process itself could cost $10,000 to $25,000 in platform fees and data costs.

facts.fact: Adwave says campaigns can launch CTV campaigns starting at just $30 a day.
facts.quote: CTV campaigns starting at just $30 a day

facts.fact: Netflix and Disney+ restrict political ads entirely under their own platform policies.
facts.quote: Some restrict political ads entirely (Netflix, Disney+)

facts.fact: California's CCPA/CPRA gives consumers opt-out rights, though political activities have some exemptions.
facts.quote: gives consumers opt-out rights, though political activities have some exemptions

facts.fact: Adwave sets a $30-a-day minimum spend for its voter data onboarding CTV campaigns.
facts.quote: With Adwave's $30-a-day minimum, even testing becomes affordable.

facts.fact: In a hypothetical example from Adwave, a state senate candidate with 80,000 registered voters in the district achieves a 65% match rate, targeting roughly 52,000 streaming households.
facts.quote: A state senate candidate with a voter file of 80,000 registered voters in their district can onboard that file, achieve a 65% match rate, and target roughly 52,000 streaming households

facts.fact: Adwave states that a clean, standardized voter file can improve match rates by 10-15 percentage points compared to a raw voter file dump.
facts.quote: A clean, standardized file can improve match rates by 10-15 percentage points compared to a raw voter file dump.

facts.fact: Appending phone numbers or email addresses to a voter file through a data vendor typically costs $0.01 to $0.05 per record.
facts.quote: The cost is typically $0.01 to $0.05 per record

facts.fact: Adwave recommends re-onboarding a voter file every 4-6 weeks during a campaign cycle.
facts.quote: Re-onboard your file every 4-6 weeks

facts.fact: Some platforms charge a flat fee of $1,000 to $5,000 for custom voter data onboarding, while others include onboarding in their CPM rates.
facts.quote: Some platforms charge a flat fee of $1,000 to $5,000 for custom onboarding

facts.fact: Traditional onboarding through LiveRamp takes 3 to 7 business days from file upload to activated audience.
facts.quote: Traditional onboarding through major platforms like LiveRamp takes 3 to 7 business days from file upload to activated audience.

facts.fact: Adwave advises budgeting 2 to 3 days for subsequent voter file onboarding refreshes.
facts.quote: budget 2 to 3 days for subsequent refreshes.

facts.fact: Campaigns have successfully onboarded voter files as small as 10,000 to 20,000 voters.
facts.quote: campaigns have successfully onboarded files as small as 10,000 to 20,000 voters.

facts.fact: In a hypothetical city council example, a 15,000-voter district with a 60% match rate yields 9,000 targetable households.
facts.quote: onboarding the full file and achieving a 60% match rate gives you 9,000 targetable households.
